introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2020. Duration: two and a half hours. Do ALL the tasks (Task 1, Task 2 and Task 3) specified in the question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three. Each version has three tasks: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task 3 (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the pictures 'foxandstork' and 'hareandtortoise' found on the desktop) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

Rien n'est imprimé sur le fait qu'un candidat ne traite qu'une seule version : regles_choix reste vide (convention des Paper 3 de pratique).

Les filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo, les cadres d'en-tête (numero de centre, nom du candidat, « For examiners' use only »), les lignes à compléter, la réponse manuscrite « Microsoft office Word 2007 » portée à la main sur la page 2 et les artefacts de scanner sont ignores. Les images « foxandstork » et « hareandtortoise » et les fichiers du bureau ne figurent pas dans le PDF.

Aucun logiciel (Word, Excel, compilateur C ou Pascal) n'a été exécuté : les menus et les étapes sont donnés de mémoire (Office récent) et ne sont pas testés. Les formules de tableur ont été traduites en Python et exécutées sur les données du sujet (COUNT, COUNTA, ROUND, AVERAGE, RANK, COUNTIF). Le code C et Pascal n'a pas été compilé : sa logique a été vérifiée par une simulation Python fidèle (mêmes entrées, mêmes sorties, cas limites).
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : les réponses sont rédigées. Les répartitions de points dans les corrigés (quand il y en a) sont indicatives ; les points imprimés du sujet ne sont jamais modifiés.

Task 2, Group One : les points imprimés sont 5 + (1+1+1+1) + 1 + (2+2+2+2) = 18, alors que l'en-tête indique 20 marks ; les lignes 5 (save) et 6 (print) n'ont pas de points imprimés. Écart du sujet laisse tel quel (points non corrigés).

Figure 2 (capture de feuille de calcul) : recadrée sans filigrane depuis la page 3, lisible. Les cellules vides (His de Njie Fabian, Mat de Verla Jones, His de Akemjia Leonard) sont lues comme des notes absentes. Le « rank » n'est pas défini : il est calculé sur la moyenne (colonne Avge), classement décroissant (rang 1 = moyenne la plus haute) ; si le jury classe selon le total, les rangs diffèrent. « Correct to 2 decimal places » : ROUND(...,2), format à 2 décimales possible.

questions.enonce_markdown: Create a workbook called Task 2 and enter the worksheet data exactly as provided.  *[5 marks]*
Use a bold font of size 14 for the title.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Click cell **A1**. In the *Home* tab, click **B** (Bold, *Ctrl + B*) and choose the font size **14**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Use a bold font of size 12 for the column headers.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the header row **A2:I2** (click A2, *Shift* + click I2). Click **B** (Bold) and choose the font size **12**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Auto fit all data columns.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the columns **A to I** (click the header of column A, *Shift* + click the header of column I). In the *Home* tab choose *Format* > **AutoFit Column Width** (or double-click the boundary between two selected column headers). Each column now takes the width of its longest entry, so that names such as *Tataw Princewill* are fully visible.

questions.enonce_markdown: Merge cells A1 to I1 and center the title.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the range **A1:I1** and click **Merge & Center** in the *Home* tab, *Alignment* group. The nine cells become one cell and the title is centred over the table.

questions.enonce_markdown: Add the following three column headers to the right of column I: **SubSat, Avge and Rank**.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Column I is the last column of the data (Econs), so the new headers go in **J2** (`SubSat`), **K2** (`Avge`) and **L2** (`Rank`). Give them the same format as the other headers (bold, size 12).

questions.enonce_markdown: For the first student Njie Fabian, use suitable spreadsheet functions (or formulas) to calculate: a) number of subjects sat.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Njie Fabian is in row 3 and his marks are in D3:I3. Type in **J3**:

`=COUNT(D3:I3)`

`COUNT` counts the cells that contain a number and ignores the empty cell (His), so the result is **5** subjects sat (Eng, Fre, Mat, Geo, Econs).

questions.enonce_markdown: For the first student Njie Fabian ... b) average (correct to 2 decimal places).  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Type in **K3**:

`=ROUND(AVERAGE(D3:I3),2)`

`AVERAGE` ignores the empty cell, so it divides the total of the marks present by the number of marks present: $(12 + 9 + 11.5 + 13 + 13.5) / 5 = 59 / 5 = 11.8$. `ROUND(...,2)` gives the answer correct to 2 decimal places: **11.80** (displayed 11.8; format the cell with 2 decimals to show 11.80). Another valid way: `=AVERAGE(D3:I3)` and then *Home* > *Increase/Decrease Decimal* to show 2 decimal places.

questions.enonce_markdown: For the first student Njie Fabian ... c) rank.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The rank is the position of the student when the averages are ordered from the highest (rank 1) to the lowest. Type in **L3**:

`=RANK(K3,$K$3:$K$12,0)`

`K3` is the value to rank, `$K$3:$K$12` is the list of all the averages (the dollar signs keep the list fixed when the formula is copied down) and `0` means descending order. Njie Fabian's average, 11.8, is beaten by 4 averages (13.42, 13.00, 12.83, 12.50), so his rank is **5**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence, calculate similar values for the other students.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **J3:L3** and drag the fill handle (small square at the bottom right corner of the selection) down to row **12** (or double-click it). The references D3:I3 and K3 move down row by row, while `$K$3:$K$12` stays the same. Results (the formulas were checked with a Python simulation on the data of Figure 2):

| Row | Student | SubSat (J) | Avge (K) | Rank (L) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Njie Fabian | 5 | 11.80 | 5 |
| 4 | Tatah Ami | 6 | 10.50 | 10 |
| 5 | Verla Jones | 5 | 13.00 | 2 |
| 6 | Mvogo Cliff | 6 | 11.17 | 8 |
| 7 | Mary Tita | 6 | 12.83 | 3 |
| 8 | Tataw Princewill | 6 | 10.92 | 9 |
| 9 | Akemjia Leonard | 5 | 11.40 | 7 |
| 10 | Ful Saradia | 6 | 12.50 | 4 |
| 11 | Ngemoussi Juliet | 6 | 13.42 | 1 |
| 12 | Kinah Queenta | 6 | 11.75 | 6 |

The averages are all different, so there is no tie in the ranks. The rank is based on the average (column K), which already takes into account the number of subjects sat.
